q: A right triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm is rotated the side of 3 cm to form a cone. The volume of the cone so formed is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Clearly}}, \\ & {\text{We have }}r = 3\,{\text{cm}}\,{\text{and}}\,h = 4\,{\text{cm}} \\ & \therefore \,\,\,{\text{Volume}} \\ & = \frac{1}{3}\pi {r^2}h \\ & = \left( {\frac{1}{3} \times \pi \times {3^2} \times 4} \right){\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = 12\pi \,{\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \end{aligned}$$

q: In a shower, 5 cm of rain falls. The volume of water that falls on 1.5 hectares of ground is:
A hall is 15 m long and 12 m broad. If the sum of the areas of the floor and the ceiling is equal to the sum of the areas of four walls, the volume of the hall is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & 2\left( {15 + 12} \right) \times h = 2\left( {15 \times 12} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow h = \frac{{180}}{{27}}m = \frac{{20}}{3}m \\ & \therefore {\text{Volume}} = \left( {15 \times 12 \times \frac{{20}}{3}} \right){m^3} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 1200\,{m^3} \end{aligned}$$

q: 66 cubic centimetres of silver is drawn into a wire 1 mm in diameter. The length of the wire in metres will be:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{length}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{wire}}\,{\text{be h}} \\ & {\text{Radius}} = \frac{1}{2}mm = \frac{1}{{20}}cm.\,{\text{Then}}, \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{22}}{7} \times \frac{1}{{20}} \times \frac{1}{{20}} \times h = 66 \\ & \Rightarrow h = {\frac{{66 \times 20 \times 20 \times 7}}{{22}}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 8400\,cm \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 84\,meters \end{aligned}$$

q: A hollow iron pipe is 21 cm long and its external diameter is 8 cm. If the thickness of the pipe is 1 cm and iron weights 8 g/cm 3 , then the weight of the pipe is:
A boat having a length 3 m and breadth 2 m is floating on a lake. The boat sinks by 1 cm when a man gets on it. The mass of the man is:
s: Volume of water displaced = (3 x 2 x 0.01) m 3 = 0.06 m 3 . ∴ Mass of man = Volume of water displaced x Density of water = (0.06 x 1000) kg = 60 kg.

q: 50 men took a dip in a water tank 40 m long and 20 m broad on a religious day. If the average displacement of water by a man is 4 m 3 , then the rise in the water level in the tank will be:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Total}}\,{\text{Volume}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{water}}\,{\text{displaced}} \\ & = \left( {4 \times 50} \right){m^3} = 200\,{m^3} \\ & \therefore {\text{Rise}}\,{\text{in}}\,{\text{water}}\,{\text{level}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{200}}{{40 \times 20}}} \right)m \\ & = 0.25\,m \\ & = 25\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: The slant height of a right circular cone is 10 m and its height is 8 m. Find the area of its curved surface.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & l = 10\,m \\ & h = 8\,m \\ & So,\,r = \sqrt {{l^2} - {h^2}} = \sqrt {{{\left( {10} \right)}^2} - {8^2}} = 6\,m \\ & \therefore {\text{Curved}}\,{\text{surface}}\,{\text{area}} \\ & \pi \,rl = \left( {\pi \times 6 \times 10} \right){m^2} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 60\pi \,{m^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: A cistern 6m long and 4 m wide contains water up to a depth of 1 m 25 cm. The total area of the wet surface is:
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Area}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{wet}}\,{\text{surface}} \\ & = \left[ {2\left( {lb + bh + lh} \right) - lb} \right] \\ & = 2\left( {bh + lh} \right) + lb \\ & = \left[ {2\left( {4 \times 1.25 + 6 \times 1.25} \right) + 6 \times 4} \right]{m^2} \\ & = 49\,{m^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: A metallic sheet is of rectangular shape with dimensions 48 m x 36 m. From each of its corners, a square is cut off so as to make an open box. If the length of the square is 8 m, the volume of the box (in m 3 ) is:
s: Clearly, l = (48 - 16)m = 32 m, b = (36 -16)m = 20 m, h = 8 m. ∴ Volume of the box = (32 x 20 x 8) m 3 = 5120 m 3

q: The curved surface area of a cylindrical pillar is 264 m 2 and its volume is 924 m 3 . Find the ratio of its diameter to its height.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{\pi \,{r^2}h}}{{2\pi \,rh}} = \frac{{924}}{{264}}\, \\ & \Rightarrow r = {\frac{{924}}{{264}} \times 2} = 7m \\ & {\text{And}},\,2\pi rh = 264 \\ & \Rightarrow h = {264 \times \frac{7}{{22}} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{7}} = 6m \\ & \therefore {\text{Required}}\,{\text{ratio}} \\ & = \frac{{2r}}{h} = \frac{{14}}{6} = 7:3 \end{aligned}$$

q: A cistern of capacity 8000 litres measures externally 3.3 m by 2.6 m by 1.1 m and its walls are 5 cm thick. The thickness of the bottom is:
s: Let the thickness of the bottom be x cm Then, $${\mkern 1mu} {\left( {330 - 10} \right) \times \left( {260 - 10} \right) \times \left( {110 - x} \right)} =$$ $$8000 \times$$ $$1000$$ $$\Rightarrow 320 \times 250 \times \left( {110 - x} \right) = 8000 \times 1000$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \left( {110 - x} \right) = \frac{{8000 \times 1000}}{{320 \times 250}} = 100 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 10\,{\text{cm}} = 1\,{\text{dm}} \end{aligned}$$

q: What is the total surface area of a right circular cone of height 14 cm and base radius 7 cm?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & h = 14\,cm,\,r = 7\,cm \\ & {\text{So}},\,l = \sqrt {{{\left( 7 \right)}^2} + {{\left( {14} \right)}^2}} = \sqrt {245} = 7\sqrt 5 \,cm \\ & \therefore {\text{Total}}\,{\text{surface}}\,{\text{area}} \\ & = \pi \,rl + \pi \,{r^2} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times 7 \times 7\sqrt 5 + \frac{{22}}{7} \times 7 \times 7} \right)c{m^2} \\ & = \left[ {154\left( {\sqrt 5 + 1} \right)} \right]c{m^2} \\ & = \left( {154 \times 3.236} \right)c{m^2} \\ & = 498.35\,c{m^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: A large cube is formed from the material obtained by melting three smaller cubes of 3, 4 and 5 cm side. What is the ratio of the total surface areas of the smaller cubes and the large cube?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Volume}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{large}}\,{\text{cube}} \\ & = \left( {{3^3} + {4^3} + {5^3}} \right) = 216\,c{m^3} \\ & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{edge}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{large}}\,{\text{cube}}\,{\text{be}}\,a \\ & So,\,{a^3} = 216\,\,\,\,\, \Rightarrow \,\,\,\,\,a = 6\,cm \\ & \therefore {\text{Required}}\,{\text{ratio}} \\ & = {\frac{{6 \times \left( {{3^2} + {4^2} + {5^2}} \right)}}{{6 \times {6^2}}}} \\ & = \frac{{50}}{{36}} \\ & = 25:18 \end{aligned}$$

q: How many bricks, each measuring 25 cm x 11.25 cm x 6 cm, will be needed to build a wall of 8 m x 6 m x 22.5 cm?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Number}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{bricks}} \\ & = \frac{{{\text{Volume}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\ text{the}}\,{\text{wall}}}}{{{\text{Volume}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{1}}\,{\text{brick}}}} \\ & = {\frac{{800 \times 600 \times 22.5}}{{25 \times 11.25 \times 6}}} \\ & = 6400 \end{aligned}$$

q: The dimensions of a cuboid are 7 cm, 11 cm and 13 cm. The total surface area is :
s: Surface area : $$\begin{aligned} & = {2\left( {7 \times 11 + 11 \times 13 + 7 \times 13} \right)} \\ & = {2 \times 311} \\ & = 622{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: Rita and Meeta both are having lunch boxes of a cuboid shape. Length and breadth of Rita's lunch box are 10% more than that of Meeta's lunch box, but the depth of Rita's lunch box is 20% less than that of Meeta's lunch box. The ratio of the capacity of Rita's lunch box to that of Meeta's lunch box is :
s: let l, b and h denote the length, breadth and depth of Meeta's lunch box Then, length of Rita's lunch box : $$= 110\% {\text{ of }}l = \frac{{11l}}{{10}}$$ Breadth of Rita's lunch box : $$= 110\% {\text{ of }}b = \frac{{11b}}{{10}}$$ Depth of Rita's lunch box : $$= 80\% {\text{ of }}h = \frac{{4h}}{5}$$ ∴ Ratio of the capacities of Rita's and Meeta's lunch boxes : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{11l}}{{10}} \times \frac{{11b}}{{10}} \times \frac{{4h}}{5}:lbh \\ & = \frac{{121}}{{125}}:1 \\ & = 121:125 \end{aligned}$$

q: A rectangular water tank is 8 m high, 6 m long and 2.5 m wide. How many litres of water can it hold ?
s: Volume of the tank : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {8 \times 100 \times 6 \times 100 \times 2.5 \times 100} \right)c{m^3} \\ & = 120000000\,c{m^3} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{120000000}}{{1000}}} \right){\text{litres}} \\ & = 120000{\text{ litres}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Total surface area of a cube whose side is 0.5 cm is :
s: Surface area : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {6 \times {{\left( {\frac{1}{2}} \right)}^2}} \right]{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = \frac{3}{2}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: A larger cube is formed from the material obtained by melting three smaller cubes of 3, 4 and 5 cm side. The ratio of the total surface areas of the smaller cubes and the larger cube is :
s: Volume of the larger cube : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {{3^3} + {4^3} + {5^3}} \right){\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = 216{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \end{aligned}$$ Let the edge of the larger cube be a cm $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {a^3} = 216 \\ & \Rightarrow a = 6 \end{aligned}$$ Required ratio : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{6\left( {{3^2} + {4^2} + {5^2}} \right)}}{{6 \times {6^2}}} \\ & = \frac{{6 \times 50}}{{6 \times 36}} \\ & = \frac{{25}}{{18}}\,Or\,25:18 \end{aligned}$$

q: The diameter of the base of a cylindrical drum is 35 dm and the height is 24 dm. It is full of kerosene. How many tins each of size 25 cm × 22 cm × 35 cm can be filled with kerosene from the drum ?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Number of tins}} \\ & = \frac{{{\text{Voulme of the drum}}}}{{{\text{Volume of each tin}}}} \\ & = \frac{{\left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times \frac{{35}}{2} \times \frac{{35}}{2} \times 24} \right)}}{{\left( {\frac{{25}}{{10}} \times \frac{{22}}{{10}} \times \frac{{35}}{{10}}} \right)}} \\ & = 1200 \end{aligned}$$

q: The radius of a cylindrical cistern is 10 metres and its height is 15 metres. Initially the cistern is empty. We start filling the cistern with water through a pipe whose diameter is 50 cm. Water is coming out of the pipe with a velocity of 5 m/sec. How many minutes will it take in filling the cistern with water ?
s: Volume of cistern : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\pi \times {{10}^2} \times 15} \right){m^3} \\ & = 1500\pi {m^3} \end{aligned}$$ Volume of water flowing through the pipe in 1 sec : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\pi \times 0.25 \times 0.25 \times 5} \right){m^3} \\ & = 0.3125\pi {m^3} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Time taken to fill the cistern : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{1500\pi }}{{0.3125\pi }}} \right) \\ & = \left( {\frac{{1500 \times 10000}}{{3125}}} \right) \\ & = 4800\,\sec \\ & = \left( {\frac{{4800}}{{60}}} \right)\min \\ & = 80\,\min \end{aligned}$$

q: What length of solid cylinder 2 cm in diameter must be taken to cast into a hollow cylinder of external diameter 12 cm, 0.25 cm thick and 15 cm long ?
s: External radius = 6 cm Internal radius = (6 - 0.25) = 5.75 cm Volume of material in hollow cylinder : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {\frac{{22}}{7} \times \left\{ {{{\left( 6 \right)}^2} - {{\left( {5.75} \right)}^2}} \right\} \times 15} \right]{\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times 11.75 \times 0.25 \times 15} \right){\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times \frac{{1175}}{{100}} \times \frac{{25}}{{100}} \times 15} \right){\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{11 \times 705}}{{56}}} \right){\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \end{aligned}$$ Let the length of solid cylinder be h Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{22}}{7} \times 1 \times 1 \times h = \left( {\frac{{11 \times 705}}{{56}}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow h = \left( {\frac{{11 \times 705}}{{56}} \times \frac{7}{{22}}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow h = 44.0625\,{\text{cm}} \end{aligned}$$

q: If the height of a right circular cone is increased by 200% and the radius of the base is reduced by 50%, then the volume of the cone :
s: Let the original radius and height of the cone be r and h respectively Then, Original volume = $$\frac{1}{3}\pi {r^2}h$$ New radius = $$\frac{r}{2}$$ and new hight = 2h New volume : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{1}{3} \times \pi \times {\left( {\frac{r}{2}} \right)^2} \times 3h \\ & = \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{3}\pi {r^2}h \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Decrease % : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{3}\pi {r^2}h}}{{\frac{1}{3}\pi {r^2}h}} \times 100} \right)\% \\ & = 25\% \end{aligned}$$

q: A bucket is in the from of a frustum of a cone and holds 28.490 litres of water. The radii of the top and bottom are 28 cm and 21 cm respectively. Find the height of the bucket.
s: Volume of bucket : = 28.490 litres = (28.490 ×1000) cm 3 = 28490 cm 3 Let the height of the bucket be h cm We have : r = 21 cm. and R = 28 cm $$\therefore \frac{\pi }{3}h\left[ {{{\left( {28} \right)}^2} + {{\left( {21} \right)}^2} + 28 \times 21} \right]$$ $$= 28490$$ $$\Rightarrow h\left( {784 + 441 + 588} \right) =$$ $$\frac{{28490 \times 21}}{{22}}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 1813h = 27195 \\ & \Rightarrow h = \frac{{27195}}{{1813}} \\ & \Rightarrow h = 15\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: If the volume and surface area of a sphere are numerically the same, then its radius is :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{4}{3}\pi {r^3} = 4\pi {r^2} \\ & \Rightarrow r = 3 \text{ units} \end{aligned}$$

q: A copper wire of length 36 m and diameter 2 mm is melted to form a sphere. The radius of the sphere (in cm) is :
s: Let the radius of the sphere be r cm Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{4}{3}\pi {r^3} = \pi \times {\left( {0.1} \right)^2} \times 3600 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {r^3} = 36 \times \frac{3}{4} \\ & \Leftrightarrow {r^3} = 27 \\ & \Leftrightarrow r = 3\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: The capacities of two hemispherical vessels are 6.4 litres and 21.6 litres. The areas of inner curved surfaces of the vessels will be in the ratio of :
s: Let their radii be R and r Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{\frac{2}{3}\pi {R^3}}}{{\frac{2}{3}\pi {r^3}}} = \frac{{6.4}}{{21.6}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\left( {\frac{R}{r}} \right)^3} = \frac{8}{{27}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\left( {\frac{R}{r}} \right)^3} = {\left( {\frac{2}{3}} \right)^3} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{R}{r} = \frac{2}{3} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Ratio of curved surface area : $$= \frac{{2\pi {R^2}}}{{2\pi {r^2}}} = {\left( {\frac{R}{r}} \right)^2} = \frac{4}{9}\,or\,4:9$$

q: The base of a pyramid is an equilateral triangle of side 1 m. If the height of the pyramid is 4 metres, then the volume is :
s: Area of the base : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{4} \times {1^2}} \right){m^2} \\ & = \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{4}{m^2} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Volume of pyramid : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{4} \times 4} \right){m^3} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{3}} \right){m^3} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{1.732}}{3}} \right){m^3} \\ & = 0.577\,{m^3} \end{aligned}$$

q: Each side of a cube is decreased by 25%. Find the ratio of the volume of the original cube and the resulting cube = ?
s: Let the side of cube = 10 cm ∴ Original volume = 10 × 10 × 10 = 1000 cm 3 Now, side of new cube : = 10 - 25% of 10 = 7.5 ∴ New volume = 7.5 × 7.5 × 7.5 = 421.875 cm 3 ∴ Required ratio : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{1000}}{{421.875}} \\ & = \frac{{1000000}}{{421875}} \\ & = \frac{{64}}{{27}}\,Or\,64:27 \end{aligned}$$

q: When a ball bounces, it rises to $$\frac{2}{3}$$ of the height from which it fell. If the ball is dropped from a height of 36 m, how high will it rise at the third bounce ?
s: Ball is dropped from the height of 36 m when the ball will rise at the third bounce ∴ Required height : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{2}{3} \times 36 \\ & = \frac{{32}}{3} \\ & = 10\frac{2}{3}\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: The sum of perimeters of the six faces of a cuboid is 72 cm and the total surface area of the cuboid is 16 cm 2 . Find the longest possible length that can be kept inside the cuboid :
s: Sum of perimeters of the six faces : $$\begin{aligned} & = 2\left[ {2\left( {l + b} \right) + 2\left( {b + h} \right) + 2\left( {l + h} \right)} \right] \\ & = 4\left( {2l + 2b + 2h} \right) \\ & = 8\left( {l + b + h} \right) \end{aligned}$$ Total surface area $$= 2\left( {lb + bh + lh} \right)$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 8\left( {l + b + h} \right) = 72 \\ & \Rightarrow l + b + h = 9 \\ & 2\left( {lb + bh + lh} \right) = 16 \\ & \Rightarrow lb + bh + lh = 8 \end{aligned}$$ Now, $${\left( {l + b + h} \right)^2} = {l^2} + {b^2} + {h^2} + 2$$ $$\left( {lb + bh + lh} \right)$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow {\left( 9 \right)^2} = {l^2} + {b^2} + {h^2} + 16 \\ & \Rightarrow {l^2} + {b^2} + {h^2} = 81 - 16 \\ & \Rightarrow {l^2} + {b^2} + {h^2} = 65 \end{aligned}$$ Required length : $$\begin{aligned} & = \sqrt {{l^2} + {b^2} + {h^2}} \\ & = \sqrt {65} \\ & = 8.05\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: The surface area of a cube is 150 cm 2 . Its volume is :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & 6{a^2} = 150 \\ & \Rightarrow {a^2} = 25 \\ & \Rightarrow a = 5 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Volume : $${a^3} = {5^3} = 125\,{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3}$$

q: If three equal cubes are placed adjacently in a row, then the ratio of the total surface area of the new cuboid to the sum of the surface areas of the three cubes will be ?
s: Let the length of each edge of each cube be a Then, the cuboid formed by placing 3 cubes adjacently has the dimensions 3a , a and a Surface area of the cuboid : $$\begin{aligned} & = 2\left[ {3a \times a + a \times a + 3a \times a} \right] \\ & = 2\left[ {3{a^2} + {a^2} + 3{a^2}} \right] \\ & = 14{a^2} \end{aligned}$$ Sum of surface area of 3 cubes : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {3 \times 6{a^2}} \right) \\ & = 18{a^2} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Required ratio : $$\begin{aligned} & = 14{a^2}:18{a^2} \\ & = 7:9 \end{aligned}$$

q: The curved surface area of a cylindrical pillar is 264 m 2 and its volume is 924 m 3 . Find the ratio of its diameter to its height.
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{\pi {r^2}h}}{{2\pi rh}} = \frac{{924}}{{264}} \\ & \Rightarrow r = \left( {\frac{{924}}{{264}} \times 2} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow r = 7\,m \end{aligned}$$ And, $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 2\pi rh = 264 \\ & \Rightarrow h = \left( {264 \times \frac{7}{{22}} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{7}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow h = 6\,m \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Required ratio : $$= \frac{{2r}}{h} = \frac{{14}}{6} = 7:3$$

q: It is required to fix a pipe such that water flowing through it at a speed of 7 metres per minute fills a tank of capacity 440 cubic metres in 10 minutes. The inner radius of the pipe should be :
s: Let the inner radius of the pipe be r metres Then, Volume of water flowing through the pipe in 10 minutes : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {\left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times {r^2} \times 7} \right) \times 10} \right]{m^3} \\ & = \left( {220{r^2}} \right){m^3} \\ & \therefore 220{r^2} = 440 \\ & \Rightarrow {r^2} = 2 \\ & \Rightarrow r = \sqrt 2 \, m \end{aligned}$$

q: Which one of the following figures will generate a cone when rotated about one of its straight edges ?
s: Answer :- A right-angled triangle.

q: If the heights of two cones are in the ratio 7 : 3 and their diameters are in the ratio 6 : 7, what is the ratio of their volumes ?
s: Let the heights of two cones be 7x and 3x and their radii be 6y and 7y respectively Then, Ratio of volume : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{\frac{1}{3}\pi \times {{\left( {6y} \right)}^2} \times 7x}}{{\frac{1}{3}\pi \times {{\left( {7y} \right)}^2} \times 3x}} \\ & = \frac{{36 \times 7}}{{49 \times 3}} \\ & = \frac{{12}}{7}\,Or\,12:7 \end{aligned}$$

q: Consider the volumes of the following 1. A parallelepiped of length 5 cm, breadth 3 cm and height 4 cm 2. A cube of each side 4 cm 3. A cylinder of radius 3 cm and length 3 cm 4. A sphere of radius 3 cm The volumes of these in the decreasing order is :
s: Volume of parallelepiped : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {5 \times 3 \times 4} \right)c{m^3} \\ & = 60\,c{m^3} \end{aligned}$$ Volume of cube : $$\begin{aligned} & = {\left( 4 \right)^3}\,c{m^3} \\ & = 64\,c{m^3} \end{aligned}$$ Volume of cylinder : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times 3 \times 3 \times 3} \right)c{m^3} \\ & = 84.86\,c{m^3} \end{aligned}$$ Volume of spare : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{4}{3} \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times 3 \times 3 \times 3} \right) \\ & = 113.14\,c{m^3} \end{aligned}$$ So, Option D is correct decreasing order

q: If three metallic spheres of radii 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm are melted to from a single sphere, the diameter of the new sphere will be :
s: Volume of new sphere : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {\frac{4}{3}\pi \times {{\left( 6 \right)}^3} + \frac{4}{3}\pi \times {{\left( 8 \right)}^3} + \frac{4}{3}\pi \times {{\left( {10} \right)}^3}} \right]{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = \left[ {\frac{4}{3}\pi \left\{ {{{\left( 6 \right)}^3} + {{\left( 8 \right)}^3} + {{\left( {10} \right)}^3}} \right\}} \right]{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = \left( {\frac{4}{3}\pi \times 1728} \right){\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = \left[ {\frac{4}{3}\pi \times {{\left( {12} \right)}^3}} \right]{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \end{aligned}$$ Let the radius of the new sphere be R Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{4}{3}\pi {R^3} = \frac{4}{3}\pi \times {\left( {12} \right)^3} \\ & \Rightarrow R = 12\,cm \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Diameter : $$\begin{aligned} & = 2R \\ & = 2 \times 12 \\ & = 24\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: The diameter of a spare is 8 cm. It is melted and drawn into a wire of diameter 3 mm. The length of the wire is :
s: Let the length of the wire be h Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \pi \times \frac{3}{{20}} \times \frac{3}{{20}} \times h = \frac{4}{3}\pi \times 4 \times 4 \times 4 \\ & \Rightarrow h = \left( {\frac{{4 \times 4 \times 4 \times 4 \times 20 \times 20}}{{3 \times 3 \times 3}}} \right)cm \\ & \Rightarrow h = \left( {\frac{{102400}}{{27}}} \right)cm \\ & \Rightarrow h = 3792.5\,cm \\ & \Rightarrow h = 37.9\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: The external and internal diameters of a hemispherical bowl are 10 cm and 8 cm respectively. What is the total surface area of the bowl ?
s: Internal radius, r = 4 cm External radius, R = 5 cm Total surface area : $$\begin{aligned} & = 2\pi {R^2} + 2\pi {r^2} + \pi \left( {{R^2} - {r^2}} \right) \\ & = 3\pi {R^2} + \pi {r^2} \\ & = \left[ {\pi \left( {3 \times 25 + 16} \right)} \right]{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times 91} \right){\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = 286{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: A pyramid has an equilateral triangle as its base of which each side is 1 m. Its slant edge is 3 m. The whole surface are of the pyramid is equal to :
s: Area of base : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{4} \times {1^2}} \right){m^2} \\ & = \frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{4}{m^2} \end{aligned}$$ Clearly, the pyramid has 3 triangular faces each with sides 3m, 3m and 1 m So, area of each lateral face : $$\begin{aligned} & = \sqrt {\frac{7}{2} \times \left( {\frac{7}{2} - 3} \right)\left( {\frac{7}{2} - 3} \right)\left( {\frac{7}{2} - 1} \right)} {m^2} \\ & \left[ {\because s = \frac{{3 + 3 + 1}}{2} = \frac{7}{2}} \right] \\ & = \sqrt {\frac{7}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{5}{2}} {m^2} \\ & = \frac{{\sqrt {35} }}{4}{m^2} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Whole surface area of the pyramid : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{\sqrt 3 }}{4} + 3 \times \frac{{\sqrt {35} }}{4}} \right){m^2} \\ & = \frac{{\sqrt 3 + 3\sqrt {35} }}{4}{m^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: A hemisphere and a cone have equal bases. If their heights are also equal, then the ratio of their curved surface will be :
s: Let, $$\begin{aligned} & OP = OQ = OR = r \\ & \therefore OR = h = r \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Curved surface area of the hemisphere = $$2\pi {r^2}$$ Curved surface area of a cone = $$\pi rl$$ Where, $$\begin{aligned} & l = \sqrt {{h^2} + {r^2}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\, = \sqrt {{r^2} + {r^2}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\, = r\sqrt 2 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Required ratio : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{2\pi {r^2}}}{{\pi rl}} \\ & = \frac{{2\pi {r^2}}}{{\pi r \times r\sqrt 2 }} \\ & = \frac{2}{{\sqrt 2 }} \\ & = \frac{{2 \times \sqrt 2 }}{{\sqrt 2 \times \sqrt 2 }} \\ & = \frac{{2\sqrt 2 }}{2} \\ & = \frac{{\sqrt 2 }}{1}\,Or\,\sqrt 2 :1 \end{aligned}$$

q: A swimming pool 9 m wide and 12 m long and 1 m deep on the shallow side and 4 m deep on the deeper side. Its volume is :
s: Given length of width of swimming pool is 9 m and 12 m respectively Volume of swimming pool : $$\begin{aligned} & = 9 \times 12 \times \left( {\frac{{1 + 4}}{2}} \right) \\ & = 9 \times 12 \times \frac{5}{2} \\ & = 270\,\text{cu. metre} \end{aligned}$$

q: A closed aquarium of dimensions 30 cm × 25 cm × 20 cm is made up entirely of glass plates held together with tapes. The total length of tape required to hold the plates together (ignore the overlapping tapes) is :
s: Total length of tape required : = Sum of lengths of edges = (30 × 4 + 25 × 4 + 20 × 4) cm = 300 cm

q: A swimming pool 9 m wide and 12 m long is 1 m deep on the shallow side and 4 m deep on the deeper side. It volume is :
s: Volume : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {12 \times 9 \times \left( {\frac{{1 + 4}}{2}} \right)} \right]{m^3} \\ & = \left( {12 \times 9 \times 2.5} \right){m^3} \\ & = 270\,{m^3} \end{aligned}$$

q: An aluminium sheet 27 cm long, 8 cm broad and 1 cm thick is melted into a cube. The difference in the surface areas of the two solids would be :
s: Volume of cube = Volume of sheet = (27 × 8 × 1) cm 3 = 216 cm 3 Edge of cube : $$\sqrt[3]{216} \,cm = 6\,cm$$ Surface area of sheet : $$\begin{aligned} & = 2\left( lb + bh + lh \right) \\ & = 2\left( {27 \times 8 + 8 \times 1 + 27 \times 1} \right){\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = \left( {216 + 8 + 27} \right){\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = 502{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \end{aligned}$$ Surface area of cube : $$\begin{aligned} & = 6{a^2} \\ & = \left( {6 \times {6^2}} \right){\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = 216{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Required difference : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {502 - 216} \right){\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = 286{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: The volumes of two cubes are in the ratio 8 : 27. The ratio of their surface areas is :
s: Let their edges be a and b Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{{a^3}}}{{{b^3}}} = \frac{8}{{27}} \\ & \Rightarrow {\left( {\frac{a}{b}} \right)^3} = {\left( {\frac{2}{3}} \right)^3} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{a}{b} = \frac{2}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{{a^2}}}{{{b^2}}} = \frac{4}{9} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{6{a^2}}}{{6{b^2}}} = \frac{4}{9}\,Or\,4:9 \end{aligned}$$

q: The height of a right circular cylinder is 6 m. If three times the sum of the areas of its two circular faces is twice the area of the curved surface, then the radius of its base is :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & 3 \times 2\pi {r^2} = 2 \times 2\pi rh \\ & \Rightarrow 6r = 4h \\ & \Rightarrow r = \frac{2}{3}h \\ & \Rightarrow r = \left( {\frac{2}{3} \times 6} \right)m \\ & \Rightarrow r = 4\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: Water flows out through a circular pipe whose internal diameter is 2 cm, at the rate of 6 metres per second into a cylindrical tank, the radius of whose base is 60 cm. By how much will the level of water rise in 30 minutes ?
s: Volume of water flown through the pipe in 30 min : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {\left( {\pi \times 0.01 \times 0.01 \times 6} \right) \times 30 \times 60} \right]{m^3} \\ & = \left( {1.08\pi } \right){m^3} \end{aligned}$$ Let the rise in level of water be h metres Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \pi \times 0.6 \times 0.6 \times h = 1.08\pi \\ & \Rightarrow h = \left( {\frac{{1.08}}{{0.6 \times 0.6}}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow h = 3\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: What is the weight of water contained in a conical vessel 21 cm deep and 16 cm in diameter ?
s: Volume of water : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times 8 \times 8 \times 21} \right){\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = 1408{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{1408}}{{1000}}} \right)kg \\ & = 1.408\,kg \end{aligned}$$

q: If the ratio of volumes of two cones is 2 : 3 and the ratio of the radii of their bases is 1 : 2, then the ratio of their height will be :
s: let their radii be x and 2x, and their heights be h and H respectively Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{\frac{1}{3} \times \pi \times {x^2} \times h}}{{\frac{1}{3} \times \pi \times {{\left( {2x} \right)}^2} \times H}} = \frac{2}{3} \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{h}{H} = \frac{2}{3} \times 4 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{h}{H} = \frac{8}{3}\,Or\,8:3 \end{aligned}$$

q: The volume of a sphere is $$2145\frac{{11}}{{21}}{\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^3}.$$ Its radius is equal to :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times {r^3} = \frac{{45056}}{{21}} \\ & \Rightarrow {r^3} = \left( {\frac{{45056}}{{21}} \times \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{7}{{22}}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow {r^3} = 512 \\ & \Rightarrow r = \sqrt[3]{512} \\ & \Rightarrow r = 8\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: A spherical ball of lead, 3 cm in diameter is melted and recast into three spherical ball. The diameter of two of these are 1.5 cm and 2 cm respectively. The diameter of the third ball is :
s: Let the radius of the third ball be R cm Then, $$\frac{4}{3}\pi \times {\left( {\frac{3}{4}} \right)^3} + \frac{4}{3}\pi \times {\left( 1 \right)^3}$$ $$+ \frac{4}{3}\pi \times {R^3}$$ $$= \frac{4}{3}\pi \times {\left( {\frac{3}{2}} \right)^3}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{{27}}{{64}} + 1 + {R^3} = \frac{{27}}{8} \\ & \Rightarrow {R^3} = \frac{{125}}{{64}} = \frac{{{{\left( 5 \right)}^3}}}{{{{\left( 4 \right)}^3}}} \\ & \Rightarrow R = \frac{5}{4} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Diameter of the third ball : $$= 2R = \frac{5}{2}cm = 2.5\,cm$$

q: The ratio of the surface area of a sphere and the curved surface area of the cylinder circumscribing the sphere is :
s: Let the radius of the sphere be r Then, radius of the cylinder = r Height of the cylinder = 2r Surface area of sphere = $$4\pi {{\text{r}}^2}$$ Surface area of the cylinder = $$2\pi {\text{r}}(2r) = 4\pi {{\text{r}}^2}$$ ∴ Required ratio : = $$4\pi {{\text{r}}^2}$$ : $$4\pi {{\text{r}}^2}$$ = 1 : 1

q: A hemispherical bowl of internal radius 12 cm contains liquid. This liquid is to be filled into cylindrical container of diameter 4 cm and height 3 cm. The number of containers that is necessary to empty the bowl is :
s: Volume of hemispherical bowl : $$= \left( {\frac{2}{3} \times \pi \times 12 \times 12 \times 12} \right)c{m^3}$$ Volume of 1 cylindrical container : $$= \left( {\pi \times 2 \times 2 \times 3} \right)c{m^3}$$ ∴ Number of containers required : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{{12 \times 12 \times 12}}{{2 \times 2 \times 3}} \\ & = 96 \end{aligned}$$

q: Length of each edge of a regular tetrahedron is 1 cm. It volume is :
s: Length of each edge of a regular tetrahedron = 1 cm Volume of regular tetrahedron : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{{a^3}}}{{6\sqrt 2 }}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = \frac{1}{{6\sqrt 2 }} \\ & = \frac{{\sqrt 2 }}{{6\sqrt 2 \times \sqrt 2 }}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = \frac{{\sqrt 2 }}{{12}}{\text{ Or }}\frac{1}{{12}}\sqrt 2 {\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \end{aligned}$$

q: The base of a right prism is a trapezium whose lengths of two parallels sides are 10 cm and 6 cm and distance between them is 5 cm. If the heights of the prism is 8 cm, its volume is :
s: Length of parallel sides of prism = 10 cm and 6 cm Height of prism = 8 cm ∴ Volume of prism : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{1}{2}\left( {10 + 6} \right) \times 5 \times 8 \\ & = \frac{1}{2} \times 16 \times 5 \times 8 \\ & = 320{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \end{aligned}$$

q: A rectangular water reservoir contains 42000 litres of water. If the length of reservoir is 6 m and breadth of the reservoir is 3.5 m, then the depth of the reservoir will be :
s: Volume of the reservoir = 42000 litres = 42 m 3 Let the depth of the reservoir be h metres then, $$\begin{aligned} & 6 \times 3.5 \times h = 42 \\ & Or,\,h = \frac{{42}}{{6 \times 3.5}} = 2\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: A cistern, open at the top, is to be lined with sheet of lead which weights 27 kg/m 2 . The cistern is 4.5 m long and 3 m wide and holds 50 m 3 . The weight of lead required is :
s: Let the depth of the cistern be h metres Then, $$\begin{aligned} & 4.5 \times 3 \times h = 50 \\ & \Rightarrow h = \frac{{50}}{{13.5}} \\ & \Rightarrow h = \frac{{100}}{{27}} \end{aligned}$$ Area of sheet required : $$\begin{aligned} & = lb + 2\left( {bh + lh} \right) \\ & = lb + 2h\left( {l + b} \right) \\ & = \left[ {4.5 \times 3 + 2 \times \frac{{100}}{{27}} \times \left( {4.5 + 3} \right)} \right]{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = \left( {13.5 + \frac{{200}}{{27}} \times 7.5} \right){\text{ }}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{27}}{2} + \frac{{500}}{9}} \right){{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = \frac{{1243}}{{18}}{\text{ }}{{\text{m}}^2} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Weight of lead : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {27 \times \frac{{1243}}{{18}}} \right)kg \\ & = \left( {\frac{{3729}}{2}} \right)kg \\ & = 1864.5\,kg \end{aligned}$$

q: The length, breadth and height of a cuboid are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. The length, breadth and height of the cuboid are increased by 100%, 200% and 200% respectively. Then the increase in the volume of the cuboid is :
s: Let the original length, breadth and height of the cuboid be x, 2x and 3x units respectively Then, original volume = (x × 2x × 3x) cu.units = 6x 3 cu.units New length = 200% of x = 2x New breadth = 300% of 2x = 6x New height = 300% of 3x = 9x ∴ New volume : = (2x × 6x × 9x) cu.units = 108x 3 cu.units Increase in volume : = (108x 3 - 6x 3 ) cu.units = (102x 3 ) cu.units ∴ Required ratio : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{102{{\text{x}}^3}}}{{6{{\text{x}}^3}}} \\ & = 17{\text{ }}\left( {{\text{Times}}} \right) \end{aligned}$$

q: A water tank is 30 m long, 20 m wide and 12 m deep. It is made of iron sheet which is 3 m wide. The tank is open at the top. If the cost of the iron sheet is Rs. 10 per metre, then the total cost of the iron sheet required to build the tank is :
s: Since the tank is open at the top, we have : Area of sheet required = Surface area of the tank $$\begin{aligned} & = lb + 2\left( {bh + lh} \right) \\ & = \left[ {30 \times 20 + 2\left( {20 \times 12 + 30 \times 12} \right)} \right]{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = \left( {600 + 1200} \right){{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = 1800{\text{ }}{{\text{m}}^2} \end{aligned}$$ Length of sheet required : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{{\text{Area}}}}{{{\text{Width}}}}} \right) \\ & = \frac{{1800}}{3}m \\ & = 600\,m \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Cost of the sheet = Rs. (600 × 10) = Rs. 6000

q: If the total length of diagonals of a cube is 12 cm, then what is the total length of the edges of the cube ?
s: Since a cube has 4 diagonals, we have : Length of a diagonal $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{12}}{4}} \right)cm \\ & = 3\,cm \end{aligned}$$ Let the length of each edge of the cube be a cm Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \sqrt 3 a = 3 \\ & or,a = \sqrt 3 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Total length of the edges of the cube = $$12\sqrt 3\,$$ cm

q: By what percent the volume of a cube increases if the length of each edge was increased by 50%
s: Let original edge = a Then, original volume = a 3 New edge : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{150}}{{100}}a \\ & = \frac{{3a}}{2} \end{aligned}$$ New volume : $$\begin{aligned} & = {\left( {\frac{{3a}}{2}} \right)^3} \\ & = \frac{{27{a^3}}}{8} \end{aligned}$$ Increase in volume : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{27{a^3}}}{8} - {a^3}} \right) \\ & = \frac{{19{a^3}}}{8} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Increase % : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{19{a^3}}}{8} \times \frac{1}{{{a^3}}} \times 100} \right)\% \\ & = 237.5\% \end{aligned}$$

q: The height of a closed cylinder of given volume and the minimum surface area is :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & V = \pi {r^2}h{\text{ and }} \\ & S = 2\pi rh + 2\pi {r^2} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\,\, = 2\pi r\left( {h + r} \right) \\ & {\text{Where, }}h = \frac{V}{{\pi {r^2}}} \\ & \Rightarrow S = 2\pi r\left( {\frac{V}{{\pi {r^2}}} + r} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow S = \frac{{2V}}{r} + 2\pi {r^2} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{dS}}{{dr}} = \frac{{ - 2V}}{{{r^2}}} + 4\pi r{\text{ and}} \\ & \frac{{{d^2}S}}{{d{r^2}}} = \left( {\frac{{4V}}{{{r^3}}} + 4\pi } \right){\text{ > 0}} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ S is minimum when : $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{dS}}{{dr}} = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{{ - 2V}}{{{r^2}}} + 4\pi r = 0 \\ & \Rightarrow V = 2\pi {r^3} \\ & \Rightarrow \pi {r^2}h = 2\pi {r^3} \\ & \Rightarrow h = 2r \end{aligned}$$

q: Water is poured into an empty cylindrical tank at a constant rate for 5 minutes. After the water has been poured into the tank. the depth of the water is 7 feet. The radius of the tank is 100 feet. Which of the following is the best approximation for the rate at which the water was poured into the tank ?
s: Volume of water flown into the tank in 5 min : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times 100 \times 100 \times 7} \right){\text{cu}}{\text{.feet}} \\ & = 220000\,{\text{cu}}{\text{.feet}} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Rate of flow of water : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{220000}}{{5 \times 60}}} \right){\text{cu}}{\text{.feet/sec}} \\ & = 733.3 \approx 700\,{\text{cu}}{\text{.feet/sec}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The curved surface of a right circular cone of height 15 cm and base diameter 16 cm is :
s: h = 15 cm, r = 8 cm So, $$\begin{aligned} & l = \sqrt {{r^2} + {h^2}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\, = \sqrt {{8^2} + {{\left( {15} \right)}^2}} \\ & \,\,\,\,\,\, = 17\,cm \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Curved surface area : $$\begin{aligned} & = \pi rl \\ & = \left( {\pi \times 8 \times 17} \right){\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \\ & = 136\pi {\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: A right circular cone and a right circular cylinder have equal base and equal height. If the radius of the base and the height are in the ratio 5 : 12, then the ratio of the total surface area of the cylinder to that of the cone is :
s: Let their radius and height be 5x and 12x respectively Slant height of the cone, $$l = \sqrt {{{\left( {5x} \right)}^2} + {{\left( {12x} \right)}^2}} = 13x$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{{{\text{Total surface area of cylinder}}}}{{{\text{Total surface area of cone}}}} \\ & = \frac{{2\pi r\left( {h + r} \right)}}{{\pi r\left( {l + r} \right)}} \\ & = \frac{{2\left( {h + r} \right)}}{{\left( {l + r} \right)}} \\ & = \frac{{2 \times \left( {12x + 5x} \right)}}{{\left( {13x + 5x} \right)}} \\ & = \frac{{34x}}{{18x}} \\ & = \frac{{17}}{9}\,Or\,17:9 \end{aligned}$$

q: The curved surface area of a sphere is 5544 sq.cm. Its volume is :
s: $$\begin{aligned} & 4\pi {r^2} = 5544 \\ & \Rightarrow {r^2} = \left( {5544 \times \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{7}{{22}}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow {r^2} = 441 \\ & \Rightarrow r = 21 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Volume : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{4}{3} \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times 21 \times 21 \times 21} \right){\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = 38808{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \end{aligned}$$

q: A hollow spherical metallic ball has an external diameter 6 cm and is $$\frac{1}{2}$$ cm thick. The volume of metal used in the ball is :
s: External radius = 3 cm Internal radius = (3 - 0.5) cm = 2.5 cm Volume of the metal : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {\frac{4}{3} \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times \left\{ {{{\left( 3 \right)}^3} - {{\left( {2.5} \right)}^3}} \right\}} \right]{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = \left( {\frac{4}{3} \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times \frac{{91}}{8}} \right){\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{143}}{3}} \right){\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = 47\frac{2}{3}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \end{aligned}$$

q: If a hollow sphere of internal and external diameters 4 cm and 8 cm respectively is melted into a cylinder of base diameter 8 cm, then the height of the cylinder is :
s: Let the height of the cylinder be h cm Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{4}{3}\pi \left[ {{{\left( 4 \right)}^3} - {{\left( 2 \right)}^3}} \right] = \pi \times {4^2} \times h \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{4}{3} \times \pi \times 56 = \pi \times 16h \\ & \Rightarrow h = \frac{{4 \times 56}}{{3 \times 16}} \\ & \Rightarrow h = \frac{{14}}{3}\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: The ratio of the volume of a hemisphere and a cylinder circumscribing this hemisphere and having a common base is :
s: Let the radius of the hemisphere be be r cm Then, radius of the cylinder = r cm Height of the cylinder = r cm ∴ Required ratio : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{{\text{Volume of hemisphere}}}}{{{\text{Volume of cylinder}}}} \\ & = \frac{{\frac{2}{3}\pi {r^3}}}{{\pi {r^2} \times r}} \\ & = \frac{2}{3}\, Or\,2:3 \end{aligned}$$

q: The volume of a right circular cone which is obtained from a wooden cube of edge 4.2 dm wasting minimum amount of wood is :
s: The volume of cone should be maximum ∴ Radius of the base of cone : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{{\text{Edge of cube}}}}{2} \\ & = \frac{{4.2}}{2} \\ & = 2.1\,{\text{dm.}} \end{aligned}$$ Height of cone = Edge of cube = 4.2 dm. ∴ Volume of cone : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{1}{3}\pi {r^2}h \\ & = \left( {\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times 2.1 \times 2.1 \times 4.2} \right){\text{cu}}{\text{.dm}}{\text{.}} \\ & = 19.404\,{\text{cu}}{\text{.dm}}{\text{.}} \end{aligned}$$

q: If the diameter of a sphere is 6 m, its hemisphere will have a volume of :
s: Volume of hemisphere : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{2}{3}\pi \times 3 \times 3 \times 3} \right){m^3} \\ & = \left( {18\pi } \right){m^3} \end{aligned}$$

q: The length of the longest rod that can be placed in a room of dimensions 10 m × 10 m × 5 m is :
s: Required length : $$\begin{aligned} & = \sqrt {{{\left( {10} \right)}^2} + {{\left( {10} \right)}^2} + {{\left( 5 \right)}^2}} \,m \\ & = \sqrt {225} \,m \\ & = 15\,m \end{aligned}$$

q: The sum of the radius and the height of a cylinder is 19 m. The total surface area of the cylinder is 1672 m 2 , what is the volume of the cylinder ?
s: Let the radius of the cylinder be r and height be h Then, r + h = 19 Again, total surface area of cylinder = $$\left( {2\pi rh + 2\pi {r^2}} \right)$$ Now, $$\begin{aligned} & 2\pi r\left( {h + r} \right) = 1672 \\ & \Rightarrow 2\pi r \times 19 = 1672 \\ & \Rightarrow 38\pi r = 1672 \\ & \therefore \pi r = \frac{{1672}}{{38}} = 44\,m \\ & \therefore r = \frac{{44 \times 7}}{{22}} = 14\,m \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Height = 19 - 14 = 5 m Volume of cylinder : $$\begin{aligned} & = \pi {r^2}h \\ & = \frac{{22}}{7} \times 14 \times 14 \times 5 \\ & = 22 \times 2 \times 14 \times 5 \\ & = 3080\,{m^3} \end{aligned}$$

q: Given that 1 cu. cm of marble weights 25 gms, the weight of a marble block 28 cm in width and 5 cm thick is 112 kg. The length of the block is :
s: Let length = x cm Then, $$\begin{aligned} & x \times 28 \times 5 \times \frac{{25}}{{1000}} = 112 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \left( {112 \times \frac{{1000}}{{25}} \times \frac{1}{{28}} \times \frac{1}{5}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow x = 32\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: An open box is made by cutting the congruent squares from the corners of a rectangular sheet of cardboard of dimension 20 cm × 15 cm. If the side of each square is 2 cm, the total outer surface area of the box is :
s: Clearly, $$l$$ = (20 - 4) cm = 16 cm b = (15 - 4) cm = 11 cm and h = 2 cm ∴ Outer surface area of the box : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {2\left( {l + b} \right) \times h} \right] + lb \\ & = \left[ {\left\{ {2\left( {16 + 11} \right) \times 2} \right\} + 16 \times 11} \right] \\ & = \left( {108 + 176} \right) \\ & = 284{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2} \end{aligned}$$

q: V 1 , V 2 , V 3 and V 4 are the volumes of four cubes of side lengths x cm, 2x cm, 3x cm and 4 cm respectively. Some statements regarding these volumes are given below : (i) V 1 + V 2 + 2V 3 < V 4 (ii) V 1 + 4V 2 + V 3 < V 4 (iii) 2(V 1 + V 3 ) + V 2 = V 4 Which of these statements area correct ?
A circular well with a diameter of 2 metres, is dug to a depth of 14 metres. What is the volume of the earth dug out ?
s: Volume : $$\begin{aligned} & = \pi {r^2}h \\ & = \left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times 1 \times 1 \times 14} \right){m^3} \\ & = 44\,{m^3} \end{aligned}$$

q: If the radius of the base of a right circular cylinder is halved, keeping the height same, what is the ratio of the volume of the reduced cylinder to that of the original one ?
s: Let original radius = R Then, new radius = $$\frac{{\text{R}}}{2}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{{{\text{Volume of reduced cylinder }}}}{{{\text{Volume of original cylinder}}}} \\ & = \frac{{\pi \times {{\left( {\frac{R}{2}} \right)}^2} \times h}}{{\pi \times {R^2} \times h}} \\ & = \frac{1}{4}\,Or\,1:4 \end{aligned}$$

q: The number of circular pipes with an inside diameter of 1 inch which will carry the same amount of water as a pipe with an inside diameter of 6 inches is :
s: Let the length of each pipe be $$l$$ inches Then, volume of water in thinner pipe : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {\pi \times {{\left( {\frac{1}{2}} \right)}^2} \times 1} \right] \text{cu.inch} \\ & = \left( {\frac{{\pi l}}{4}} \right)\text{cu.inch} \end{aligned}$$ Volume of water in thinker pipe : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\pi \times {3^2} \times l} \right)\text{cu.inch} \\ & = \left( {9\pi l} \right)\text{cu.inch} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Required number of pipes : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{9\pi l}}{{\left( {\frac{{\pi l}}{4}} \right)}} \\ & = 36 \end{aligned}$$

q: A right triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm is rotated about the side of 3 cm to form a cone. The volume of the cone so formed is :
s: Clearly, we have r = 3 cm and h = 4 cm ∴ Volume : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{1}{3}\pi {r^2}h \\ & = \left( {\frac{1}{3} \times \pi \times {3^2} \times 4} \right)\pi {r^3} \\ & = 12\pi {\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \end{aligned}$$

q: The radius of the base and height of a metallic solid cylinder are r cm and 6 cm respectively. It is melted and recast into a solid cone of the same radius of base. The height of the cone is :
s: Let the height of the cone be h cm Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \pi \times {r^2} \times 6 = \frac{1}{3} \times \pi \times {r^2} \times h \\ & \Rightarrow h = 18\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: For a sphere of radius 10 cm, What percent of the numerical value of its volume would be the numerical value of the surface area ?
s: Volume of the sphere : $$= \left[ {\frac{4}{3}\pi {{\left( {10} \right)}^3}} \right]{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3}$$ Surface area of the sphere : $$= \left[ {4\pi {{\left( {10} \right)}^2}} \right]{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^2}$$ ∴ Required percentage : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {\frac{{4\pi {{\left( {10} \right)}^2}}}{{\frac{4}{3}\pi {{\left( {10} \right)}^3}}}} \times 100 \right]\% \\ & = 30\% \end{aligned}$$

q: How many lead shots each 3 mm in diameter can be made from a cuboid of dimensions 9 cm × 11 cm × 12 cm ?
s: Volume of each lead shot : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {\frac{4}{3}\pi \times {{\left( {\frac{{0.3}}{2}} \right)}^3}} \right]{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = \left( {\frac{4}{3} \times \frac{{22}}{7} \times \frac{{27}}{{8000}}} \right){\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = \frac{{99}}{{7000}}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Number of lead shots : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {9 \times 11 \times 12 \times \frac{{7000}}{{99}}} \right) \\ & = 84000 \end{aligned}$$

q: A metallic sphere of radius 5 cm is melted to make a cone with base of the same radius. What is the height of the cone ?
s: Let the height of the cone be h cm Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{4}{3}\pi \times {\left( 5 \right)^3} = \frac{1}{3}\pi \times {\left( 5 \right)^2} \times h \\ & \Rightarrow h = 20\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: A hemisphere of lead of radius 6 cm is cast into a right circular cone of height 75 cm. The radius of the base of the cone is :
s: Let the radius of the cone be R cm Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{3}\pi \times {R^2} \times 75 = \frac{2}{3}\pi \times 6 \times 6 \times 6 \\ & \Rightarrow {R^2} = \left( {\frac{{2 \times 6 \times 6 \times 6}}{{75}}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow {R^2} = \frac{{144}}{{25}} \\ & \Rightarrow {R^2} = \frac{{{{\left( {12} \right)}^2}}}{{{{\left( 5 \right)}^2}}} \\ & \Rightarrow R = \frac{{12}}{5} \\ & \Rightarrow R = 2.4\,cm \end{aligned}$$

q: Base of a right prism is a rectangle, the ratio of whose length and breadth is 3 : 2. If the height of the prism is 12 cm and total surface area is 288 sq.cm the volume of the prism is :
s: Let the length of base be 3a cm and breadth be 2a cm Total surface area of prism : = [Perimeter of base × height] + [2 × Area of base] = [2 (3a + 2a) × 12 + 2 × 3a × 2a] sq.cm = (120a + 12a 2 ) sq.cm According to the question, 120a + 12a 2 = 288 ⇒ a 2 + 10a = 24 ⇒ a 2 + 10a - 24 = 0 ⇒ a 2 + 12a - 2a - 24 = 0 ⇒ a (a + 12) - 2 (a + 12) = 0 ⇒ (a - 2)(a + 12) = 0 ⇒ a = 2 because a $$\ne$$ -12 ∴ Volume of prism : = Area of base × Height = (3a × 2a × 12)cu.cm = 72a 2 cu.cm = (72 × 2 × 2)cu.cm = 288 cu.cm

q: A patient in a hospital is given soup daily in a cylindrical bowl of diameter 7 cm. If the bowl is filled with soup to a height of 4 cm, how much soup the hospital has to prepare daily to serve 250 patients ?
s: Diameter of bowl = 7 cm ∴ Radius of bowl = $$\frac{2}{7}$$ cm Height = 4 cm ∴ Volume of cylindrical bowl : $$\begin{aligned} & = \pi {r^2}h \\ & = \frac{{22}}{7} \times \frac{7}{2} \times \frac{7}{2} \times 4 \\ & = 154\,cu.cm \end{aligned}$$ Hence, volume of soup for 250 patients : $$\begin{aligned} & = 154 \times 250 \\ & = 38500{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = 38.5{\text{L}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The breadth of a room is twice its height and half its length. The volume of the room is 512 cu.m. The length of the room is :
s: Let the height of the room be x metres Then, breadth = 2x metres and length = 4x metres ∴ Volume of the room : = (4x × 2x × x) m 3 = (8x 3 ) m 3 8x 3 = 512 ⇒ x 3 = 64 ⇒ x = 4 ∴ Length of the room is : = 4x = (4 × 4) = 16 m

q: A closed box made of wood of uniform thickness has length, breadth and height 12 cm, 10 cm and 8 cm respectively. If the thickness of the wood is 1 cm, the inner surface area is :
s: Internal length = (12 - 2) cm = 10 cm Internal breadth = (10 - 2) cm = 8 cm Internal height = (8 - 2) cm = 6 cm Inner surface area : = 2 [10 × 8 + 8 × 6 + 10 × 6] cm 2 = (2 × 188) cm 2 = 376 cm 2

q: From a cube of side 8 m, a square hole of 3 m side is hollowed from end to end. What is the volume of the remaining solid ?
s: Volume of the remaining solid : = Volume of the cube - Volume of the cuboid cut out from it = [(8 × 8 × 8) - (3 × 3 × 8)] m 3 = (512 - 72) m 3 = 440 m 3

q: The dimensions of a rectangular box are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4 and the difference between the cost of covering it with sheet of paper at the rate of Rs. 8 and Rs. 9.50 per square metre is Rs. 1248. Find the dimensions of the box in metres.
s: Let the length, breadth and height of the box be 2x, 3x and 4x respectively Then, surface area of the box : = 2 [2x.3x + 3x.4x + 2x.4x] = [2(6x 2 + 12x 2 + 8x 2 )] = 52x 2 $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 52{x^2} = \frac{{1248}}{{1.50}} \\ & \Rightarrow 52{x^2} = 832 \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} = \frac{{832}}{{52}} \\ & \Rightarrow {x^2} = 16 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 4 \end{aligned}$$ Hence, the diameter of the box are 8 m, 12 m and 16 m

q: A cuboidal water tank contains 216 litres of water. Its depth is $$\frac{1}{3}$$ of its length and breadth is $$\frac{1}{2}$$ of $$\frac{1}{3}$$ of the difference between length and depth. The length of the tank is :
s: Let the length of the tank be x dm Then, depth of the tank = $$\frac{x}{3}$$ dm Breadth of the tank : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {\frac{1}{2}{\text{ of }}\frac{1}{3}{\text{ of }}\left( {x - \frac{x}{3}} \right)} \right]{\text{dm}} \\ & = \left( {\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{{2x}}{3}} \right){\text{dm}} \\ & = \frac{x}{9}\,{\text{dm}} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore x \times \frac{x}{9} \times \frac{x}{3} = 216 \\ & \Rightarrow {x^3} = 216 \times 27 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 6 \times 3 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 18\,dm \end{aligned}$$

q: A covered wooden box has the inner measures as 115 cm, 75 cm and 35 cm and the thickness of wood is 2.5 cm. Find the volume of the wood :
s: The external measures of the box are (115 + 5) cm, (75 + 5) cm, and (35 + 5) cm i.e., 120 cm, 80 cm and 40 cm Volume of the wood : = External volume - Internal volume = [(120 × 80 × 40) - (115 × 75 × 35)] cm 3 = (384000 - 301875) cm 3 = 82125 cm 3

q: Find the cost of a cylinder of radius 14 m and height 3.5 m when the cost of its metal is Rs. 50 per cubic meter :
s: Volume : $$\begin{aligned} & = \pi {r^2}h \\ & = \left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times 14 \times 14 \times 3.5} \right){m^3} \\ & = 2156\,{m^3} \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Cost of the cylinder : $$\begin{aligned} & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {2156 \times 50} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. 107800}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The radii of the bases of two cylinders are in the ratio 3 : 4 and their height are in the ratio 4 : 3. The ratio of their volume is :
s: Let their radii be 3x, 4x and heights be 4y, 3y Ratio of their volumes : $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{\pi \times {{\left( {3x} \right)}^2} \times 4y}}{{\pi \times {{\left( {4x} \right)}^2} \times 3y}} \\ & = \frac{{36}}{{48}} \\ & = \frac{3}{4}\,Or\,3:4 \end{aligned}$$

q: Find the number of coins 1.5 cm in diameter and 0.2 cm thick, to be melted to form a right circular cylinder of height 10 cm and diameter 4.5 cm.
s: Volume one coin : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times \frac{{75}}{{100}} \times \frac{{75}}{{100}} \times \frac{2}{{10}}} \right){\text{c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \\ & = \frac{{99}}{{280}}{\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3} \end{aligned}$$ Volume of larger cylinder : $$= \left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times \frac{9}{4} \times \frac{9}{4} \times 10} \right){\text{ c}}{{\text{m}}^3}$$ Number of coins : $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{22}}{7} \times \frac{9}{4} \times \frac{9}{4} \times 10 \times \frac{{280}}{{99}}} \right) \\ & = 450 \end{aligned}$$
